lines.text: A three-digit number can change what you pay for a car, an apartment, and even a phone plan.
lines.say: A three-digit number can change what you pay for a car, an apartment, and even a phone plan.

lines.text: It's your credit score. Today we're going to take it apart, piece by piece, so you know exactly how it works.
lines.say: It's your credit score. Today we're going to take it apart, piece by piece, so you know exactly how it works.

lines.text: Chapter one. What a credit score actually is.
lines.say: Chapter one. What a credit score actually is.

lines.text: A credit score is a number that sums up how reliably you've paid back money you borrowed.
lines.say: A credit score is a number that sums up how reliably you've paid back money you borrowed.

lines.text: The most widely used one, the FICO score, runs from 300 to 850.
lines.say: The most widely used one, the FICO score, runs from three hundred to eight hundred fifty.

lines.text: It's calculated from your credit reports, which are kept by three big credit bureaus.
lines.say: It's calculated from your credit reports, which are kept by three big credit bureaus.

lines.text: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.
lines.say: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.

lines.text: Your credit report is the record. Your score is a grade calculated from that record.
lines.say: Your credit report is the record. Your score is a grade calculated from that record.

lines.text: And you don't have just one score. There are different models, like FICO and VantageScore, and lenders pick which one they use.
lines.say: And you don't have just one score. There are different models, like FICO and VantageScore, and lenders pick which one they use.

lines.text: Why it matters: a higher score can mean lower interest rates, smaller deposits, and more yeses when you apply.
lines.say: Why it matters: a higher score can mean lower interest rates, smaller deposits, and more yeses when you apply.

lines.text: Chapter two. The five things that make up your score.
lines.say: Chapter two. The five things that make up your score.

lines.text: FICO publishes how much each part counts. Here's the whole recipe.
lines.say: FICO publishes how much each part counts. Here's the whole recipe.

lines.text: Payment history is the biggest piece, at thirty-five percent. Amounts owed is next, at thirty.
lines.say: Payment history is the biggest piece, at thirty-five percent. Amounts owed is next, at thirty.

lines.text: Together, those two are almost two-thirds of your score. So let's start there.
lines.say: Together, those two are almost two-thirds of your score. So let's start there.

lines.text: Chapter three. Payment history.
lines.say: Chapter three. Payment history.

lines.text: This one is simple: do you pay your bills on time?
lines.say: This one is simple: do you pay your bills on time?

lines.text: A payment usually gets reported as late once it's thirty days past due.
lines.say: A payment usually gets reported as late once it's thirty days past due.

lines.text: And a late payment can stay on your credit report for up to seven years.
lines.say: And a late payment can stay on your credit report for up to seven years.

lines.text: Paying a day or two late usually means a late fee, not a hit to your credit report. The thirty-day mark is what counts.
lines.say: Paying a day or two late usually means a late fee, not a hit to your credit report. The thirty-day mark is what counts.

lines.text: If you do miss one, pay it as fast as you can. The longer it goes, the worse it gets, at sixty and ninety days.
lines.say: If you do miss one, pay it as fast as you can. The longer it goes, the worse it gets, at sixty and ninety days.

lines.text: The easiest fix is autopay for at least the minimum, so a busy week never becomes a late payment.
lines.say: The easiest fix is autopay for at least the minimum, so a busy week never becomes a late payment.

lines.text: Chapter four. Amounts owed.
lines.say: Chapter four. Amounts owed.

lines.text: A big part of this is your credit utilization.
lines.say: A big part of this is your credit utilization.

lines.text: If your limit is five thousand dollars and you owe one thousand, you're using twenty percent.
lines.say: If your limit is five thousand dollars and you owe one thousand, you're using twenty percent.

lines.text: Lower usage generally helps your score. Here's how the same five thousand dollar limit looks at different balances.
lines.say: Lower usage generally helps your score. Here's how the same five thousand dollar limit looks at different balances.

lines.text: A common rule of thumb is to stay under thirty percent, and lower is better.
lines.say: A common rule of thumb is to stay under thirty percent, and lower is better.

lines.text: Paying your balance before the statement date can also lower the number that gets reported.
lines.say: Paying your balance before the statement date can also lower the number that gets reported.

lines.text: The good news: card balances are usually reported monthly, so paying them down can show up in your score fairly quickly.
lines.say: The good news: card balances are usually reported monthly, so paying them down can show up in your score fairly quickly.

lines.text: Chapter five. The last three pieces.
lines.say: Chapter five. The last three pieces.

lines.text: Length of history is fifteen percent. Older accounts help, so closing your oldest card can shorten your history.
lines.say: Length of history is fifteen percent. Older accounts help, so closing your oldest card can shorten your history.

lines.text: New credit covers hard inquiries.
lines.say: New credit covers hard inquiries.

lines.text: A hard inquiry stays on your report for two years, and FICO scores only count it for about one year.
lines.say: A hard inquiry stays on your report for two years, and FICO scores only count it for about one year.

lines.text: Shopping around for a mortgage or car loan? Scoring models usually count several of those checks in a short window as one.
lines.say: Shopping around for a mortgage or car loan? Scoring models usually count several of those checks in a short window as one.

lines.text: Opening several new cards at once is different. It adds inquiries and lowers the average age of your accounts.
lines.say: Opening several new cards at once is different. It adds inquiries and lowers the average age of your accounts.

lines.text: And credit mix means having different kinds, like a card and an installment loan. It's the smallest piece, so never borrow just to improve it.
lines.say: And credit mix means having different kinds, like a card and an installment loan. It's the smallest piece, so never borrow just to improve it.

lines.text: Chapter six. Checking your credit, for free.
lines.say: Chapter six. Checking your credit, for free.

lines.text: You can get free credit reports from all three bureaus every week at AnnualCreditReport dot com.
lines.say: You can get free credit reports from all three bureaus every week at AnnualCreditReport dot com.

lines.text: Checking your own credit is a soft inquiry, so it doesn't hurt your score.
lines.say: Checking your own credit is a soft inquiry, so it doesn't hurt your score.

lines.text: Look for accounts you don't recognize or payments marked late by mistake, and dispute errors with the bureau.
lines.say: Look for accounts you don't recognize or payments marked late by mistake, and dispute errors with the bureau.

lines.text: Chapter seven. Starting from zero.
lines.say: Chapter seven. Starting from zero.

lines.text: If you have no credit history, you can't have a score yet. Here are the common ways people start.
lines.say: If you have no credit history, you can't have a score yet. Here are the common ways people start.

lines.text: Whichever you use, the same rules apply: small balances, paid on time, every month.
lines.say: Whichever you use, the same rules apply: small balances, paid on time, every month.

lines.text: Chapter eight. Myths that cost people money.
lines.say: Chapter eight. Myths that cost people money.

lines.text: Myth: you need to carry a balance and pay interest to build credit.
lines.say: Myth: you need to carry a balance and pay interest to build credit.

lines.text: Fact: paying your full balance still shows on-time payments and low usage. You never have to pay interest to build credit.
lines.say: Fact: paying your full balance still shows on-time payments and low usage. You never have to pay interest to build credit.

lines.text: Myth: a higher income means a higher score. Fact: income isn't part of your credit score at all.
lines.say: Myth: a higher income means a higher score. Fact: income isn't part of your credit score at all.

lines.text: Myth: closing an unused card always helps. It can actually hurt, because your total limit shrinks and your usage goes up.
lines.say: Myth: closing an unused card always helps. It can actually hurt, because your total limit shrinks and your usage goes up.

lines.text: Chapter nine. How long the bad stuff lasts.
lines.say: Chapter nine. How long the bad stuff lasts.

lines.text: Late payments and collections can stay for up to seven years. Some bankruptcies stay for up to ten.
lines.say: Late payments and collections can stay for up to seven years. Some bankruptcies stay for up to ten.

lines.text: But their impact fades. Recent on-time payments matter more than old mistakes.
lines.say: But their impact fades. Recent on-time payments matter more than old mistakes.

lines.text: So here's the whole thing in five moves.
lines.say: So here's the whole thing in five moves.

lines.text: Pay on time. Keep balances low. Keep old accounts open. And apply only when you need to.
lines.say: Pay on time. Keep balances low. Keep old accounts open. And apply only when you need to.

lines.text: And check your reports every few months, for free, so nothing surprises you.
lines.say: And check your reports every few months, for free, so nothing surprises you.

lines.text: Do those consistently, and your score takes care of itself over time.
lines.say: Do those consistently, and your score takes care of itself over time.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
